stem.en: Potassium chloride, one of the salts in ORS, is an ionic compound. It is tested with the bulb when solid, when dissolved in water and when molten at 770 °C. What happens, and why?

text.en: Dark when solid, glows when dissolved and when molten, because the ions are free to move in both liquids.
Glows when solid, because the ions are packed close together, and dark in both liquids, because they spread apart.
Dark when solid and when molten, and glows when dissolved, because only water can free the ions.
Dark when solid, glows when dissolved and when molten, because dissolving and melting make new ions.

explanation.en: Potassium chloride is like common salt: its ions are fixed in the solid and free to move in a liquid. Option b has it backwards, because ions packed in a crystal cannot travel however close they are. Option c forgets molten salt, which conducts with no water. Option d gives the right results for the wrong reason: the ions were already in the solid, and dissolving or melting only sets them free.

hints.en: Ask two questions for each state: are ions present, and are they free to move?
